prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 2 "Hole drilling": indemnified in 1 of 3 earlier cases, t = 0 in 2; when indemnified t per pc about 70 (80% range 52 to 107); revealed per pc: >=64 (case 14)
- line 8 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 16 of 32 earlier cases, t = 0 in 16; when indemnified t per pc about 80 (80% range 73 to 88); revealed per pc: >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39), >=71 (case 40), >=82 (case 43), >=81 (case 44)
- line 9 "Skilled worker hours": indemnified in 3 of 7 earlier cases, t = 0 in 4; when indemnified t per hr about 43 (80% range 33 to 59); revealed per hr: 35-42 (case 24), 35-40 (case 26), 50-58 (case 36), so this line (14 hr) about 599 (458 to 821)
- line 12 "Removal and disposal of damaged insulation": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 74 (80% range 55 to 113); revealed per pc: >=68 (case 21)
- line 19 "Rock wool pipe insulation": indemnified in all 3 earlier cases; when indemnified t per m about 22 (80% range 18.3 to 26); revealed per m: >=22 (case 39), >=19.4 (case 40), >=19.0 (case 44)
- line 20 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in all 4 earlier cases; when indemnified t per unit about 60 (80% range 55 to 66); revealed per unit: >=57 (case 18), 58-61 (case 40), >=58 (case 43), >=57 (case 44)

items.rationale: The tiling panel was directly affected by water from the insured escape of water event; reinstatement of the same kind and quality is owed under 7.1.1(b) and 1.3. Only the damaged area is covered (3 m² matches the described panel).
Drilling a hole through a new tile for the pipe is necessary for reinstatement of the damaged panel (7.1.5, 5.2.6). Reference price per pc about 70 (range 52–107).
Material for reinstating the damaged tiled panel, same kind and quality as before (plain white, DIY range). Covered under 7.1.1(b), but not as an upgrade.
Levelling material for rebuilding the patch of render that was soft/damaged by water, necessary for reinstatement (7.1.5).
No such tile size exists; likely a mis-entry or unrelated to the described repair. No evidence these were used in the reinstatement of the damaged area (3.5(e)).
Silicone joints in the internal corner and end of the panel are necessary for reinstatement (described as part of the original finish). Covered under 7.1.1(b).
Only standard-grade materials are covered (3.5(a)); premium sealant is not indemnified beyond the cost of standard silicone. Allow standard cost for the necessary length (matches line 6).
Travel charge for the contractor, reimbursed once per document (7.4.2). Reference cases: t per pcs about 80 (range 73–88).
Labour for reinstatement of the damaged area, covered at local rates (7.4.1). Reference: 14 hrs about 599 (range 458–821).

items.description: Clean wall tile covering 1 flat rate
items.rationale: Cleaning of the reinstated surface within the damage area is part of the repair cost (3.5(c)).
Removal of the wet plasterboard boxing next to the damage area is covered if it was affected by the water (damage description confirms this).

items.description: Removal and disposal of damaged insulation 1 pcs
items.rationale: Removal and disposal of sodden mineral wool from the boxing is necessary due to water damage (5.1(a), 5.2.1). Reference: t per pcs about 74 (range 55–113).

items.description: Remove damp plaster in basement rooms 3 m²
items.rationale: Removal of damp render behind the tiled panel is necessary for reinstatement (damage description matches 3 m²). Covered under 7.1.1(b).

items.description: Remove damp plaster in attic 1 pcs
items.rationale: Attic gable plaster was not affected by this insured event; removal is unrelated maintenance (3.5(b)).
Replacement of the chrome cover ring (wall rosette) broken during necessary repair is covered as part of reinstatement (7.1.1(b)).
Disassembly/reassembly of the pipe joint and fittings was necessary to stop the leak and reinstate the system (7.1.1(b)).
Drying of the affected area is covered under 5.2.7. Reference: 7 days about 403 (case 39).
No evidence this is a necessary or attributable cost for reinstatement (7.4.4 requires attribution). Usually not indemnified unless specifically justified.
Replacement of sodden lagging on the pipe is necessary for reinstatement (damage description, 7.1.1(b)). Reference: t per m about 22 (range 18.3–26).
Disposal of debris from the reinstatement is covered under 5.1(a), 5.2.1. Reference: t per unit about 60 (range 55–66).
